overview: White brings the queen out to d3 on move two, an odd move that blocks the d-pawn and the c1 bishop's path to nothing in particular. It aims for Nc3 and e4 or a London-like build with the queen on d3. The main sideline is 2...Nc6 3.Nc3 (Siberian Attack). Black usually develops freely and is comfortable.

white_ideas.idea: Develop the knights and play e4 with the queen well placed on d3
Provoke a surprise and avoid mainstream theory

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Nf6, ...Nc6 and ...e5 and take the centre

typical_structures.structure: d4/d5 with the white queen on d3 in front of the d-pawn

character.notes: Unforced and rather slow; no clear forcing lines.

soundness.notes: Not refuted but strong players think the queen is misplaced.

structure.notes: Centre pawns facing each other, undecided.

approach.notes: Played almost never at strong level, a surprise.

level.notes: Not a first repertoire choice since Black can easily gain the better game.

sublines_that_differ.name: Siberian Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: Black develops the knight and White continues with the plan of e4.

character.reason: Slow, unforced play with no clear risk either way.

soundness.reason: The early queen on d3 is considered inferior but not refuted.

structure.reason: The d-pawns face each other and the centre is undecided.

level.reason: A dubious line, so never Beginner.

plans.reason: The queen comes out on move two.
